description.narrative: Output 1.1: Increased capacity of NSAs to support LCMs, RWs and SRFs on ESG and to contribute to the development and implementationof ESG policies and practices, that comply with international standards, especially of the Vietnamese rubber sector. A.1.1.1 Organise trainings for NSAs on ESG, including relevant international standards and EU policies, and topics such as, gender equality, gender action learning system (GALS), Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC)2 and advocacy skills and tools. A.1.1.2Organise trainings of trainers (ToTs) for NSA members to support LCMs, RWs and SRFs on ESG policies and practices, including their rights and obligations. A 1.1.3 Support NSAs to engage in provincial and national multi-stake holder workshops and advocacy events to promote evidence-based policy recommendations arising from the Action. (link with op 1.3) A 1.1.4 Support NSAs to have dialogues with EU and others, e.g. Team Europe Initiative (TEI) on Sustainability in Global Value Chains, the EU-VN DAG, relevant embassies of EU Member States, UNWG on BHR, and UN Global Compact to promote evidence-based policy recommendations arising from the Action and inform EU initiatives surrounding in sustainable global value chains (link with op 1.3) Output 1.2: Increased knowledge of LCMs, RWs and SRFs, especially women, of their rights and improved capacity to contribute to, and monitor the development and implementation of ESG policies and practices in the Vietnamese rubber sector. A.1.2.1 Trainings by NSAs for key LCMs, RWs and SRFs, especially women, (henceforth core members), on ESG, gender equality GALS, FPIC, land rights, labour rights, and social protection. A.1.2.2 Training by NSAs for core members on FPIC, monitoring skills and tools, community facilitation and coaching A.1.2.3 NSAs support core members to work with other LCMs, RWs and SRFs to develop and implement initiatives alongside local authorities and private enterprises related to ESG policies and practices. A.1.2.4 Organise dialogues between LCMs, RWs, SRFs, LAs, rubber SMEs and lead firms. A 1.2.5 Organise exchange and learning among LCMs, RWs, SRFs and NSAs Output 1.3: Increased cooperation between multiple stakeholders at provincial and national levels, within which NSAs have trusted roles and effectively contribute to ESG policies and practices of the Vietnamese rubber sector, that comply with international standards. A.1.3.1 Organise trainings and workshops on ESG policies and practices, including relevant international standards and EU policies for LAs. A.1.3.2 Organise workshops on ESG policies and practices, including relevant international standards and EU policies for national government bodies A.1.3.3 Organise local multi-stakeholder meetings and dialogues on the development and implementation of ESG guidelines and regulations that meet national and relevant international standards, including applicable EU policies A.1.3.4 Organise national multi-stakeholder meetings and dialogues on the development and implementation of national ESG policies that comply with relevant international standards and EU policies A.1.3.5 Support joint initiatives of multi-stakeholder members in developing, implementing, and monitoring national ESG policies and plans and ensuring they align with relevant international standards including applicable EU policies, through FSTP A.1.3.6 Establish and facilitate multi-stakeholder working groups or platform (offline and online) on ESG policies and practices, particularly among SMEs and communicate learnings to relevant platforms at local, national and EU levels (e.g. TEI, EU - VN DAG) A1.3.7. Organise an award for SMEs and NSAs on promoting ESG best practices and report widely in media to promote NSAs and private enterprises working together on ESG practices in the Vietnameserubber sector. Output 2.1: Increased capacity of SRFs, particularly women and EM farmers to negotiate for economically, socially, and environmentally sustainable contracts with rubber companies, and to adopt ESG standards that comply with national policies and relevant international standards. A.2.1.1 Support SRFs to organise into cooperatives and/or collaborative groups A.2.1.2 Organise trainings on cooperative management, business operations, contract negotiations with rubberSMEs A.2.1.3 Organise technical trainings on ESG compliance, including applicable EU standards, with a particular focus on land/forest management, traceability, transparency, and due diligence A.2.1.4. Organise technical support in integrating indigenous knowledge in restoring forest biodiversity, and sustainable plantation (maximise organic inputs, reduce/reuse/recycle plastic waste, and reducing CO2 emission) A.2.1.5 Organise exchange and learning among cooperatives/ collaborative groups A.2.1.6 Document best ESG practices of SRFs/ cooperatives/ collaborative groups and share with other SRFs and VRA Output 2.2: An artificial intelligence (AI)-app based traceability tool, linked with Geographic Information System (GIS) mapping is developed and operated to support SRFs access to ESG information and enhance the transparency and traceability of their rubber operations. A.2.2.1 Map out existing initiatives on ESG transparency/traceability, and gaps in ESG information and compliance of SRFs A.2.2.2 Design and pilot an AI-app based traceability tool, linked with GIS mapping, with active engagement of smallholder rubber farmers, SMEs and VRA A.2.2.3 Operate and promote the AI-app based traceability tool and support smallholder rubber farmers to use theapp to access to ESG information and improve transparency and traceability of their rubber operation. A.2.2.4 Support VRA to operate and promote the AI-app based traceability tool nationwide. Output 2.3 Increased capacity of targeted rubber SMEs in thetwo provinces, particularly women- led SMEs to consult with LCMs, RWs, SRFs and NSAs on their ESG policies and practices to support compliance with national ESG policies and relevant international standards A.2.3.1 Organise trainings on national ESG policies and plans and relevant international standards including applicable EU policies. A.2.3.2 Provide coaching to rubber SMEs to review their existing procedures and guidelines and their implementation, including remedy mechanisms and check they align with relevant international standards including applicable EU policies A.2.3.3 Organise trainings for SMEs on conducting dialogues with LCMs and RWs and support these SMEs to pilot and organise community consultation to resolve potential and existing conflicts withLCMs and RWs A 2.3.4 Facilitate sustainable and fair cooperation between SMEs and SRFs to adopt ESG standards and policies, including relevant international standards and applicable EU policies, applying the AI-app based traceability tool to improve transparency and traceability between SMEs and SRFs. A.2.3.5 Organise exchange and learning among SMEs on opportunities, challenges and solutionsto apply ESG standards and policies, including relevant international standards and applicable EU policies of their business operations. A.2.3.6 Document good ESG practices of rubber SMEs and share with other SMEs, lead firms, VRA and VCCI and relevant bodies Output 2.4 Increased commitment of lead rubber firms and business associations i.e., VRG and VRA to adopt ESG and promulgate guidance on these standards for the Vietnamese rubber supply chain that comply with ESG national policies and relevant international standards. A.2.4.1 Organise trainings on national ESG standards and policies, including relevant international standards and applicable EU policies, with a particular emphasis on transparency and traceability in supply chains. A.2.4.2 Provide coaching and support to rubberlead firms, VRG, VRA to review and develop their strategies/policies, plans and guidelines adopting ESG standards and policies, including relevant international standards.

participating-org.narrative: Established in 2015, Centre for Highland Natural Resource Governance Research (CEGORN) is a Science and Technology organization under the Vietnam Union of Science and Technology Associations (VUSTA). CEGORN has its operation focus on matters related to policy andlaw, involving activities to raise people’s awareness. It embraces great respect and appreciation towards indigenous knowledge, presented by its efforts and investment in analysis and integration of indigenous culture into actions to promote sustainable development. In addition to great hands-on experience in working with people of ethnic minorities, CEGORN staff are all well equipped with thorough understanding about women's rights, thereby, encourage them to raise their voices and contribute to promote gender equality. In terms of project management, CEGORN has its capacity to harness resources, which contributes to enhance the effectiveness of the project implementation.
